hook.text: Camels and llamas make antibodies with no light chains — just a single heavy chain. They are tiny and tough.

buildup.text: The antigen-binding domain is just 15 kDa — one-tenth the size of a regular antibody. It is called a nanobody.

discovery.text: Nanobodies penetrate tissues that full antibodies cannot reach — including solid tumors and the blood-brain barrier.

twist.text: They survive boiling and stomach acid — opening the door to oral and inhaled biologic drugs.

climax.text: Cablivi, the first approved nanobody, treats blood clotting disorders — camelid biology becomes human medicine.

punchline.text: From llama blood to human drugs — nanobodies are small but mighty.

quiz.question: What makes nanobodies different from conventional antibodies?
options: They are synthetic chemicals, not proteins
They are ten times smaller, more stable, and derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies
They can only be used in veterinary medicine
